nary_nodes.label: Stabbing in Covent Garden
evidence: A woman was arrested after four men were stabbed in Covent Garden, a busy area of central London popular with tourists, in a suspected "mental health related incident", police said Wednesday.

A 47-year-old woman was arrested on suspicion of possession of an offensive weapon and assault," London's Metropolitan Police said in a statement posted on X.

nary_nodes.label: Police response to stabbing
evidence: Emergency services were called to the incident around 12:30pm local time (1130 GMT).
Witnesses working in a nearby restaurant said police had used tasers to arrest the woman, who was known locally as a homeless person who regularly frequented the area.

nary_nodes.label: Victims taken to hospital
evidence: The four victims – aged 34, 39, 42, and 52 – were taken to hospital where two remained with injuries not "believed to be life-threatening or life changing," the force added. The two other men attacked were discharged within hours.

nary_nodes.label: Police statement on incident
evidence: "While still at an early stage of the investigation, we would like to reassure the community that we currently believe this to be an isolated mental health related incident," Met Chief Superintendent Jason Stewart said in a brief statement.

evidence: "They (police officers) were chasing away the lady who had a knife in her hand," waiter Ahmad – who declined to give his surname – told AFP.
"I saw the lady get tased (tasered) by the police, it was the only way they could get her to drop the knife."
